correctness.rationale: The equivalence \(x_v=1-x_{p(v)}\) (or \(x_v=1\) for unattacked vertices) exactly enforces stable semantics and proves the component phase theorem for all finite indegree-one digraphs. Each even-cycle component contributes \(2+2y^{s}\) to ordered pair disagreement. Labelled cycles of rooted trees give \(\exp(\sum_{j\ge1}(T(z)^{2j}+T(zy)^{2j})/j)=Q(z)Q(zy)\). Lagrange inversion gives the exact coefficients; singularity transfer gives \(q_m\sim e^m/(2\sqrt{2\pi m})\) and \([z^n]Q(z)^2\sim e^n/8\). Endpoint mass control through \(q_m\le C e^m/\sqrt{m+1}\) proves the full weak arcsine limit, beyond a local estimate. Exhaustive independent checker: 8,496 finite checks through five vertices.

value.rationale: The exact full disagreement enumerator goes beyond the known stable-extension count and generic decision complexity. Its component-size subset-sum structure makes all attainable and repeated distances computable, while the exact mapping ensemble exhibits a non-Gaussian U-shaped limiting disagreement fraction, mathematically distinguishing likely near-agreement and near-total-conflict configurations. The particular uniform-triple weighting arises naturally from simultaneously counting a framework and two coherent viewpoints; its limitation is made explicit.
